title: The boundary half of Singer's question: horizon dynamics, blind-tested per-configuration laws, and the method-dependence of the refined-Gribov scale in SU(2) lattice ensembles (Part II)
description: Part II of an SU(2) orbit-space programme (Part I: doi:10.5281/zenodo.21993866). All quantities are Landau-gauge and gauge-dependent. Across nine GPU runs we measure the infrared gluon propagator on up to eight momentum shells at four lattice spacings, with per-configuration arrays. Established: (1) a per-configuration localization law - configurations nearer the Gribov horizon carry a less coherent lowest Faddeev-Popov mode - holds 17-of-17 in sign, +17.2 sigma combined; (2) the first-copy gauge ambiguity is quantified (scatter across 6 random-start gauge fixings is 0.249 of the ensemble scatter), validating distribution-shape claims; (3) the horizon edge is not a single universality class: lambda_min skew is positive across f1 = 0.38-0.70 and flips sign to -0.63 at f1 = 0.90, replicated across two independent runs. A frozen zero-parameter activation curve was tested blind on 42 ensembles: 41 are consistent (chi2 = 44.1/41, p = 0.34), one fails at +4.41 sigma on the largest sample ever taken in that region, withdrawing the previously published plateau value -0.51..-0.53; no replacement shape is claimed, and an audit recorded here shows the deviation is not independently corroborated (other five points 1.6 sigma) and is degenerate with a coupling effect (every point with f1 > 0.85 is at beta = 2.6). A refined-Gribov-Zwanziger scale consistent with published RGZ fits is present once the box resolves it; its spacing-independence is method-dependent and unresolved. Eleven intermediate conclusions were refuted, withdrawn, or closed unresolved by pre-registered tests and preserved in place, including two caught by this record's own audits of its authors (count regenerated by analysis/regen_tallies.py, not asserted). Not shown: the Yang-Mills mass gap, any gauge-invariant mass, any continuum limit. Research by Nitin Pandey in close collaboration with Claude (Anthropic).
